name: Blanc's Violet
lede: Blanc's Violet is a dim, blue-leaning violet from Robert Ridgway's 1912 color dictionary, and its closest relative in our whole color graph is another color from the very same book, Dauphin's Violet.

sections.title: A pair from the same book
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 “Color Standards and Color Nomenclature” lists Blanc's Violet at hex #665888 among the names he credits to a person [1]. Blanc is a French surname, and several nineteenth-century writers on color and art carried it, but Ridgway names none of them, so which Blanc the color honors is undocumented in our sources [1]. The 1955 Inter-Society Color Council catalog repeats the name in the block it calls moderate violet [1].

Its nearest neighbor in our color graph is not a basic hue word at all but [[dauphin-s-violet|Dauphin's Violet]], only 3.2 units away and almost the same, another Ridgway name from the same person-named group [1]. [[deep-soft-bluish-violet|Deep Soft Bluish Violet]] and [[haematoxylin-violet|Haematoxylin Violet]] sit a little further out [1]. Against the basic color words it reads closest to [[purple|Purple]], 11.2 units off, a wider gap than most of its named neighbors [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive matches this violet in 0.05% of 23,781 paintings, 12 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 5 [2]. That makes it rarer than 75% of the named colors in our set [2]. The sample is too thin for a reliable century, painter or country figure [2]. Our earliest match dates to 1340, by Pietro Lorenzetti, 572 years before Ridgway's 1912 book recorded the name, a floor rather than a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a color match in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment [2].
